chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub al-Khazzaz, from Abu Hamza, who said:

I saw Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) move his lips when he intended to go out, while he was standing at the door. So I said, 'I saw you moving your lips when you went out. Did you say anything?' He said, 'Yes.'

Indeed, when a person exits from his house, he should say when he intends to go out: 'Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Greatest' three times. 'By Allah I exit, and by Allah I enter, and upon Allah I rely' three times.

'O Allah, open up goodness for me in this direction of mine, and end it for me with goodness, and protect me from the evil of every creature You seize by its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on the Straight Path.'
He would remain in the guarantee of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, until Allah returns him to the place from which he came.
Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Hamza — similar to it.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite when leaving the house in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes a specific litany of dhikr and supplication to be recited while standing at the threshold, highlighting the transition from the private sphere to the public as a moment requiring divine safeguarding. The emphasis on 'Bil-Lahi akhruj' (I exit by Allah's leave) and 'Al-Lahi atawakkal' (I rely on Allah) underscores the Shia theological principle of integrating immediate reliance on God with practical action, ensuring the believer remains under Allah's protection until their safe return.
